title: Left exact functors commute with good upper truncation
statement: Let F:C->D be an additive functor between abelian categories and K a cochain complex. The mapped truncated complex F(tau<=q K) is zero above q, so its own truncation inclusion is invertible. Its inverse followed by truncation of F of the inclusion defines a canonical comparison to tau<=q(FK), compatible with the full inclusions. If F preserves finite limits, this comparison is an isomorphism.

source.document: Stacks Project, Derived Categories and Homology

proof.text: Construct the comparison as the inverse of the source truncation inclusion followed by truncation of the mapped inclusion. Naturality gives its compatibility with inclusions. Below q both inclusions are invertible. At q, the coordinate formula for the truncation inclusion identifies it with a kernel; preservation of kernels gives a unique isomorphism commuting with it. Above q both terms are zero. Apply the componentwise isomorphism criterion. Below the cut use the upstream CochainComplex.isIso_ιTruncLE_f; no local duplicate is needed.

def mapTruncLEComparison (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (q : ℤ) :
    (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (K.truncLE q) ⟶
